A1.justification: Both 16-page PDFs describe Prompt Depth Anything and contain corresponding main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original depth-estimation and reconstruction evaluations, ablations, vehicle-LiDAR demonstrations and robotic-grasping outcomes, including Tables 1–5 and appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including evaluations of the proposed method and its variants, and revises one baseline's numerical results.

M1.justification: The prompt-fusion architecture, LiDAR simulation, Zip-NeRF pseudo-depth generation, losses and inference procedure are unchanged. Section 3.3 adds references to possible reconstruction alternatives but does not report adopting them.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same HyperSim, ARKitScenes, ScanNet++, SHIFT/Waymo, diverse-scene and robotic-grasping coverage. No training or evaluation population, task or input scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark tables, ablations and applications. Lotus already appears in v1's Table 1; its revised scores do not introduce a new comparator. Newly cited methods are not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: The stated splits, resolutions, training budgets, zero-shot categories, RANSAC alignment, metrics and application settings remain unchanged, including Appendices C–E. Neither PDF explains the Lotus score revision through a changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Tables 3 and 5 and the appendices retain the same architecture, initialization, training-data, loss, resolution and reconstruction-quality analyses. Figure 7 retains the same qualitative scenarios and findings.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged: both present the same kinds of point estimates and grasping success rates, without adding seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises Lotus's zero-shot, RANSAC-aligned ARKitScenes L1/RMSE pairs: 0.0853/0.1793 becomes 0.0624/0.0970 at 384×512; 0.1038/0.1782 becomes 0.0621/0.0962 at 768×1024; and 0.1941/0.2741 becomes 0.0622/0.0965 at 1440×1920. This substantially lowers one baseline's reported errors under unchanged stated settings. The proposed method's scores, other result entries and overall leadership remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The DPT feature definitions, edge-aware loss in Equations 1–2 and metric definitions in Tables 6–7 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same prompting novelty, accurate 4K metric-depth, benchmark superiority and downstream-application claims. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and the long-range LiDAR and temporal-flickering limitations remain unchanged. Section 3.3's brief statement that more effective alternatives can be applied supplies literature pointers without a substantive new mechanism explanation, applicability boundary or specific limitation.

D1.justification: Implementation, optimization, frame filtering, computational cost, baseline alignment, vehicle preprocessing and robot details remain unchanged in Section 3.4 and the appendices. The project link and promised processed-data release are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Eight references are added, including stereo-matching papers, Guo et al.'s multi-view reconstruction, EnvGS and Street Gaussians. Two are removed: Jung et al.'s geometry-data paper and Park and Jeon's A Simple Yet Universal Framework for Depth Completion. These are limited citation changes; the central positioning and distinction from Depth Prompting remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds one short sentence about alternative approaches in Section 3.3 and updates citations and the arXiv version stamp. The remaining prose and the main-text and appendix organization are essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Several Figure 7 panels have lower embedded image resolution while retaining the same scenes and predictions. Citation additions produce limited text and bibliography reflow. Figures and tables otherwise retain their organization; Table 1's numerical revisions do not change its structure.

improvement.justification: The principal empirical revision is the unexplained replacement of six Lotus errors in Table 1. The PDFs do not establish whether these values correct an error or reflect an undocumented evaluation difference, so improved comparison accuracy cannot be assumed. The literature additions provide limited context, while the method, analyses and reproducibility documentation remain unchanged; a reliable net quality improvement cannot be established.
